data.content_ref: inline:The target misrepresents Popper by characterizing his methodology's preference as 'inductive' and as 'acknowledging its own lack of logical foundation,' then claiming 'Popper's system survives by admitting this gap as a pragmatic necessity.' Popper's critical rationalism was explicitly designed to provide a purely logical (deductive) solution to the problem of induction, via the asymmetry of falsification and verification. He openly embraced methodological conventions (rules of the game of science), but denied those conventions were inductive, pragmatic fudge-factors, or admissions of a logical gap. The target conflates Popper's methodological conventions—which he argued were logically motivated—with pragmatic conventionalism that concedes an inductive shortfall Popper himself rejected. The countercondition 'If Popper explicitly denied any conventional element in his methodology' is therefore malformed: Popper did NOT deny conventional elements, but he DID deny that those conventions were inductive or lacked logical foundation. Since that countercondition will never trigger (Popper embraced conventions), it fails to guard against the actual misattribution—namely, saddling Popper with an inductive 'gap' he explicitly denied existed.
